subject: Model fit & pilot plan — Datacove (post-call summary)

Subject: Model fit & pilot plan — Datacove (post-call summary)

Hi Liam — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and recommended next steps from our call: 

Summary of fit (short):
- Primary workload: extraction + routing + short-form summarization (avg prompt ~120 tokens, occasional long context 600–1,200 tokens).
- Key SLOs you called out: p99 latency <= 400ms for short prompts, ability to sustain ~100 TPS for bursty traffic, and tight quality on label-level extraction (F1 target > 0.92).

Redwood model recommendations (first-pass):
- redwood/llama2-13b-q4f16 (balanced quality/cost) — recommended for extraction with tuned prompt templates.
- redwood/gpt-medium-8b-q5 (lower cost, good for routing and summarization when paired with prompt filters).
- fallback: redwood/gpt-xlarge-33b-fp16 for edge cases requiring the highest precision.

Verified performance highlights (summary):
- Llama2-13b on A100-80GB equivalent: sustained 140 TPS (batching) for short prompts (<=128 tokens). Latency: p50 ~ 26ms, p95 ~ 105ms, p99 ~ 210ms.
- GPT-medium-8b quantized: sustained 320 TPS, p50 ~ 18ms, p95 ~ 62ms, p99 ~ 140ms.
(Full profiles attached and linked below; numbers are measured on the Redwood hosted runtime with our KV/prefix caching enabled.)

Artifacts & links:
- Benchmark pack (profiles + raw traces): https://app.redwood-inference.com/benchmarks/datacove-2026-11
- Prompt sets (example extraction templates): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0Bz_datacove_promptsets

Concerns / regression guardrails:
- Long-context p99s rise significantly beyond 512 tokens; we recommend a hybrid approach that routes long-context requests to the larger variant and uses prefix caching for repeated documents.
- We should lock a small regression prompt set (10–15 cases) to watch for extraction F1 drift after any model or quantization change.

Proposed next steps (mutual action):
1) Shared pilot: 2-week sandbox with 100K tokens/day simulated load from Datacove (we'll provide the infra + monitoring). Deliverables: performance profile, extraction quality report, and a cost/throughput recommendation.
2) Kickoff: target next Monday for pilot start — please confirm availability.
3) Procurement: I'll loop in procurement contacts and attach a simple MVP scope and estimated monthly footprint.

Attachments: datacove_model_recs.pdf, redwood_verified_profiles.csv, datacove_mvp_map.pdf

Thanks — I copied Jonas for technical latency/TPS follow-ups.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com

If you can send a short one-pager on the long-context latency behavior we can share with our infra lead and procurement.

Hi Liam — quick technical note on long-context behavior and TPS: 

- Llama2-13b (q4f16) long-context (512–1,024 tokens) on our standard host shows median token generation latencies that scale roughly linearly with sequence length. Measured on the same infra we quoted earlier, typical numbers:
  • 512-token input, short (<=128 token) output: p95 ~ 320ms, p99 ~ 560ms.
  • 1,024-token input, 200-token output: p95 ~ 640ms, p99 ~ 1,050ms.

- Those p99s assume network + kernel variance; enabling KV/prefix caching for repeated documents reduces p95/p99 for subsequent requests by ~25–35% depending on hit rate. For your workload (many repeated documents with small edits), caching tends to be effective.

- TPS notes: the 140 TPS figure is with moderate batching (continuous batching window of ~20ms) plus prefix caching enabled on short prompts. If you expect sustained low-latency 100 TPS with cold prefixes, plan for provisioning 2× that capacity to handle variance and scheduled maintenance windows. For burst tolerance we recommend a target provisioning of 200–250 TPS headroom (can use autoscaling policies to keep costs down).

I attached the CSV export of the verified profiles and a latency heatmap for 512–2,048 token ranges so you can share with infra.

Attachments: redwood_verified_profiles.csv, latency_heatmap_512to2048.png

Happy to hop on a 20-minute call with your infra engineer to walk through the heatmap if helpful.

—
Jonas Weber

Operational ask for kickoff:

- Share a primary infra contact (name + email) for a short call to exchange network details.
- Procurement: I've attached a small MVP scope (datacove_mvp_map.pdf) and included a DocuSign procurement link for an initial sandbox order: https://crm.redwood-inference.com/deals/DC-2026-00123/sign.
